edges.description: Loss of myophosphorylase activity blocks the first step of muscle glycogen breakdown.
Failure to mobilize glycogen deprives contracting muscle of a major early-exercise fuel.
Inability to mobilize muscle glycogen produces the hallmark exercise intolerance.
Exertional glycolytic energy failure produces muscle cramps.
Exertional muscle-energy failure can lead to muscle injury and rhabdomyolysis.
intermediate_mechanisms: exertional muscle-fiber energy depletion and injury, particularly in the first minutes of exercise

edges.description: Rhabdomyolysis releases myoglobin, producing recurrent myoglobinuria.
intermediate_mechanisms: exertional rhabdomyolysis releasing myoglobin into the circulation

edges.description: Ongoing muscle-fiber injury raises serum creatine kinase.
intermediate_mechanisms: sarcolemmal injury releasing creatine kinase into serum
